P1.evidence: P1a hit, and among the best in the batch — the rep had demonstrably read the setter's notes and used them three separate times: 'Kim gave me some context. So, you've been working out like weighted calisthenics for a while, yeah?', then 'from Kim, he told me, like, you've been, what's been missing is a little bit of structure. Is that correct?', then the rapport-building 'I remember Kim asked you, like, you're from Bahia, right?' He also opened by acknowledging the prospect's situation — 'I know you're juggling a lot with the hospital schedule and family.' P1b partial and the thinnest frame in the batch: 'Before we dive in, just want to make sure I actually understand your situation. So, before we get into any details about the program.' That is one of four parts plus a sequencing promise; where he wants to go, what is in the way and what he needs were all unframed. P1c hit — 'Cool?' asked and answered. P1d miss, and it is a direct consequence of P1a going well: having read the notes, the rep opened with closed confirmation questions off those notes rather than an open invitation. There is no version of 'what are you looking for help with' or 'brief me in your own words' anywhere on this call. It worked out because the prospect is articulate and volunteered freely, but the script credits asking.

P2.evidence: P2a partial — height, weight and age were all volunteered inside other answers and none was asked; the rep did however ask the more useful question for this prospect, 'Have you measured your fat tissue?', which produced 13-14% and a 10-12% target. P2b hit — occupation came from the setter notes and was then properly explored: 'you as a doctor, you probably work long hours, or not?' followed by the actual daily shape of the schedule. P2c miss — no health conditions or hereditary screen at all. P2d hit and promptly asked at the right moment: the prospect mentioned joint discomfort and the rep interrupted with 'Sorry to interject, did you had any injuries doing that?' P2e hit, and the best moment of the baseline: given a tangled answer about rotating splits, the rep refused to accept it — 'Jesus Christ, I got lost. So how many days do you work out per week, every day?' — and got a usable picture. P2f hit — current results were established in detail, both the wins (69 kg to 86 kg, 8-12 pull-ups with +20 kg) and the deficits (VO2 max, endurance, mobility). P2g hit — 'tell me about nutrition, how does it look like right now?', then the cheat-meal probes, which surfaced the fasting protocol. P2h miss, and conspicuously: sleep was never asked, on a physician with a two-year-old and a newborn due — and sleep deprivation is exactly the obstacle the prospect himself raised forty minutes later as the reason the programme might not work in October. P2i partial — energy was touched only inside the body-fat exchange, never established as a baseline.

P3.evidence: P3a hit — the one-thing question was asked with a time horizon attached: 'which one of these would be the most important thing for you? Like in six months, if you had to choose.' P3b hit and near-verbatim, offering the menu explicitly: 'You mentioned VO2 max, conditioning, mobility, probably too. So which one of these would be the most important thing for you?' P3c miss — never asked what he wants to do physically and cannot. P3d hit, and it was the single most productive question on the call: 'Why conditioning is so important?' opened the entire life context — busy doctor, second child coming, shrinking free time. P3e hit — 'if we get it dialed in, get you a structure, a proper plan... when you think about, what would be different? How would you operate if you would have the dial-in?' P3f partial — 'What does your wife say about it?' is a good adjacent question about support rather than impact, and the impact on the daughters was asserted by the rep in the pitch rather than asked. P3g partial — kids, marriage and the long run all appeared and the prospect supplied the material himself ('I don't want to be doing bicep curls when I'm 50'); the rep echoed rather than drove. P3h hit — an accurate, confirmed reflect-back: 'just to summarize, you told me that you've been missing some pieces, that you've been researching that, and there's been a lot of noise out there... and that the missing piece was the conditioning and mobility part and getting more VO2 max, but at the same time you build a solid strength for yourself with the heavy calisthenics.'

P4.evidence: The second clean sweep of this phase in the batch, both by the same rep in two days. P4a and P4b hit — the full training history was elicited and so was its consequence: high-volume grinding calisthenics produced joint ache and stiffness, which forced the switch to low-volume work. P4c, P4d and P4f were all delivered by one exceptionally well-built question at 00:17:10, which is the scripted 'information isn't the problem' move adapted precisely to this prospect: 'you clearly have, like, you know your stuff, yeah? So you've researched training extensively, and you've been doing this for years. So what's held you back from getting that conditioning and mobility piece dialed in on your own?' Asking a research-obsessed doctor why his own research has not solved it is exactly right, and it is the same move the rep failed to run on Jared Lyons the previous day. P4e hit — the prospect named his own gap cleanly and twice: 'mainly for me is structure, is combining with what to do, in what day, for how long, and what to do' and 'there's a lot of noise in the fitness industry. [With] structure, you can reduce that. So I believe that is what I'm lacking right now.' Getting the prospect to say the word 'structure' unprompted is the phase landing perfectly.

P5.evidence: Not run in any form — no two-year question, no settling question, no 'why not', no line in the sand. The material was on the table and unused: the prospect twice described losing ground, 'a lot of stuff that seems that I was losing through time, just by having only one goal', and closed it with 'I'm not really satisfied with that.' That is an invitation to ask what another two years of the same looks like, at 33, with a second child arriving and less time than ever. Instead the rep moved straight from the reflect-back into the three pillars. This is the recurring pattern across the batch and it matters most here, because when the price landed there was no accumulated cost of inaction for it to be weighed against — only a currency conversion.

P6.evidence: P6a partial — the belief question was never asked in the scripted form. The nearest approach, at 00:24:09, tests willingness rather than belief: 'if we could build a system that would fit around your hospital working hours and that could preserve your calisthenics and actually give you the conditioning and mobility, is this something that you're really actually wanting to commit right now?' P6b hit, verbatim and correctly placed before any number: 'if you had all those three things, like the structure, kettlebell programming built around your calisthenics, the nutrition dialed in, and someone who is in your corner supporting you all the way, would there be any reason you wouldn't commit to this?' The answer was 'Mainly cost', and the rep isolated immediately with 'Apart from that' — producing a clean 'I don't think there is another variable that concerns me.' That is the phase working. P6c partial — a second commitment check ran before pricing ('if you can figure out the details, the investment side, you're fully committed to showing up and doing the work?' / 'Yeah. I'm really looking forward to that'), which is correct sequencing. But the prospect had already named cost as the blocker fifteen minutes earlier, and the rep proceeded to the number without doing anything to pre-frame it or return to Phase 5 — which had never been run. Knowing the objection in advance and walking into it unprepared is the shortfall here.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — two tiers priced, four payment structures offered, a down payment requested — but no agreement to buy was obtained, so payment collection, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement signature and the welcome sequence were all unreachable. Scored N/A rather than miss so the phase does not double-count the unresolved affordability objection.

objection_plays.detail: Good structure, no financial picture. ISOLATE FIRST ran twice and cleanly — first inside the Phase 6 check ('Mainly cost' / 'Apart from that'), then again after the number: 'just make sure, apart from the finances right now, is there anything standing in a way from moving forward?' The payment door was opened with real, specific structures rather than vagueness — two payments of $3,000, three- and six-payment plans, and the six-pay total of $7,200 named out loud — and the rep proactively disclosed that instalments cost more, which no other call in this batch does and which is genuinely good practice. He then down-sold to the three-month tier at $4,000 with its own splits. The strongest single move came at 00:55:30: 'be transparent. Like, how much would you be actually willing to put down today? Just to see how it looks like.' That is the right question and it failed only because the prospect genuinely did not know. What never ran: permission for an open financial conversation, and every one of the six financial-picture items — cash on hand, monthly surplus after bills, number of credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, and crypto or investments. He learned the qualitative picture (renovation commitments, incoming childcare costs, school fees, a temporary income dip) and never converted it into numbers, so the down-payment question arrived with nothing behind it.

The clearest single coaching miss in this batch. The trigger was explicit at 00:45:06 — 'I have to take a little moment to think about that and involve the wife because we have a lot of projects now for this year' — and the wife was never mentioned again across the remaining twenty-three minutes. Not one move ran: no 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you there', no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger', no offer to include her on the follow-up, and no deposit-with-refund fallback. What makes it costly is that the rep had already done the hard part in discovery: he knew the wife is a doctor who runs, does CrossFit and trains three to four times a week, and who gets frustrated when she cannot train twice a week. That is a spouse who would plainly endorse the purchase, and the rep had her profile in hand and did not use a word of it. He also never suggested she join the 29 June call, despite the prospect having framed the decision as joint.

Triggered twice and handled unevenly. The first trigger was the pregnancy window — 'August, September, and October will be difficult months... training will be kept to a minimum, or maybe even severely impaired.' The rep's opening move was the wrong one, waving it away with the accountability pillar ('that's why Trevor is for you there when life gets busy'), and the prospect corrected him: 'I don't believe it's actually busy. I believe it's actually probably not only busy, but tiredness and lack of sleep... sometimes we're two or three days without sleeping well.' His recovery was genuinely good and unscripted: rather than arguing, he restructured the offer to fit the available window — 'we're in almost June. So it's June, July, August, and you have a lot of time till October. We could do the three months.' That is the right instinct and it deserves credit. The second trigger was the deferral request, and there he ran the play's core question well — 'what's going to change between now and sometime in the future?' Not run: 'things never slow down', 'when does it actually become the right time', 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', and 'the only thing you can control is right now'. The last of these had obvious purchase on a man who had just said he does not know what his finances look like after October.

Trigger present — 'I have to take a moment to think about that' and later 'Is there a possibility that I could get in touch with you after some time?' To his credit the rep did not simply grant it: he asked what would change, asked for a timeframe, and asked what the prospect would put down today, which is three consecutive attempts to convert a delay into a decision. None of the scripted lines ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to [goal]', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here, when do you make a different decision', no closing 'are you sure? Nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?' The outcome is a call booked a full month out with no deposit, no interim commitment and nothing for the prospect to do in between, against his own statement that his finances will not clarify until after October.

SCRIPT GAP — foreign currency conversion, and this is now the third occurrence in four sales calls in this batch. 'When we make the conversion it's about probably something along the lines of 25 to 28,000 [reais]' for $6,000, and on the reduced tier, 'it's a lot for right now, even 4K, because that will mean something close to 20,000.' The rep did not acknowledge the conversion once. The same gap appeared with a New Zealand prospect converting to NZ$7,500 and with a Danish prospect weighing $9,000 against local salaries. Primal is selling a flat USD price into markets with very different purchasing power and the playbook has no move for it, no regional pricing, and no framing that addresses it. On this call it is the sole reason a textbook-ICP physician did not buy.

SECOND SCRIPT GAP — a dated life event with a real physiological consequence, as distinct from the generic busyness Objection D is built for. A newborn arriving in the last week of October is not an excuse, it is a scheduled period of sleep deprivation that the prospect has already lived through once. Objection D's moves ('are you ever going to have another Thanksgiving?', 'things never slow down') are actively wrong here and would have read as dismissive, which is exactly what happened when the rep reached for the accountability pillar. What is needed and does not exist: a documented pause or hold mechanism, or a start date deliberately timed to the window before the birth. The rep improvised the second of those and it was the right answer — it simply arrived attached to a price the prospect could not pay.

THIRD GAP, recorded because it was handled well without a script — training compatibility. The prospect's stated primary condition was that he keep progressing weighted calisthenics: 'that would be my primary will is to combine those things. To not lose the gains in strength in calisthenics.' No play exists for a prospect who fears the programme will displace training he already values. The rep answered it properly and twice: 'the kettlebell days and calisthenics days, they complement each other naturally. So you don't have to replace anything that you've built. You're adding the pieces that you've been actually missing', and then with proof from Trevor's own content showing pull-ups, dips and leg raises. The objection resolved — the prospect visibly relaxed his own requirement, 'it could be calisthenics, like raw calisthenics bodyweight... it's fine.' Worth codifying as a play, since it will recur with any prospect who already has a training identity.

notes: Strong discovery, no urgency, and a loss to currency rather than to selling. The front two-thirds are among the best in the batch: setter notes genuinely used, a baseline that refused to accept vague answers, the full goals phase run properly, and a clean sweep on root cause built around one excellent question — asking a research-obsessed physician why his own research has not solved the problem. He also took commitment before the number and isolated the objection cleanly. Three things to coach. First, Phase 5 was not run at all, and this prospect handed over the material for it twice by describing capacity he has been losing over time; with no cost of inaction established, the price had nothing to be weighed against. Second, the wife objection was raised and completely ignored, despite the rep already knowing she is a CrossFitting doctor who trains three to four times a week — the most winnable spouse objection in the corpus, left untouched, and she was not invited to the follow-up. Third, the follow-up was set a month out with no deposit and no interim step, against the prospect's own statement that clarity will not arrive until after October; a booked call in five months with a deposit today would have been the stronger ask. Escalate above the rep: this is the ICP's headline occupation — a physician — declining on affordability purely because $6,000 converts to R$25,000-28,000. That is the third foreign-currency loss in four sales calls in this batch and there is no play, no framing and no regional pricing for it.
